summary: API throttler feedback loop causing surge in 5xx errors and streaming session drops for PaperTrail Labs
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway for traffic belonging to PaperTrail Labs' dedicated tenant. Errors manifested as HTTP 502/503 from the gateway and abrupt streaming session terminations. Impact: Customer-facing failures for PaperTrail's realtime chat product (multiple streams dropped, reconnect storms). Scale: Affected roughly 6% of the tenant's requests during the spike window (~10:30-11:15 PDT), with short bursts peaking at ~18% error rate. Business impact: user-facing errors and automated client retries resulting in support escalations. Timeline: - 2026-03-10 03:37 UTC: Monitoring alert triggers (gateway 5xx rate increased). - 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC: Support opened ticket; customer reports streaming disconnects. - 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: On-call SRE and ingress engineer pulled into Slack (#support and #incidents). - 2026-03-10 04:20 UTC: Initial mitigation applied (per-route rate cap lowered, soft-evict enabled). - 2026-03-10 05:00 UTC: Errors reduced but intermittent reconnect spikes continued. Observed behavior: - Connection drops reported by clients (RST/ERR stream close). - Gateway logs show short-lived upstream 502/503 with runtime returning 'upstream closed' and 'watchdog timeout' traces. - Traffic pattern: mix of short streaming sessions and frequent small inference requests; many clients retried within short backoffs. Steps to reproduce: see steps_to_reproduce field. Immediate mitigation: temporarily reverted a recent per-tenant throttler tuning deployed 2026-03-09 and increased keepalive pool size for the tenant's route. Result: immediate drop in 5xx rate to baseline, but long-tail reconnect churn persisted. Root cause hypothesis: A feedback loop between the gateway per-route token-bucket throttler and the serving-runtime backoff behavior. When the throttler began rejecting bursts, clients retried aggressively; those retries congested the ingress priority-shedder and caused rapid ephemeral connections that pushed runtimes into kernel-level timeouts and watchdog restarts under memory pressure. Secondary contributors: - Slightly aggressive throttler hysteresis (reduction window too large) introduced oscillation. - Autoscaler thresholds for the dedicated pool were tuned high for CPU (not socket backlog), so scale-up lagged. - A recent runtime patch changed reconnection jitter behavior, reducing effective jitter and concentrating retries. Current status: Mitigations in place; monitoring and customer observing. Next steps: - Engineering to introduce jittered exponential backoff in runtime client retry logic (PR created). - Tune token-bucket parameters to shorter window and lower reject penalty. - Adjust autoscaler to consider accept-queue length and open socket count. - Post-incident follow-up: write a runbook entry and bake tests for throttler hysteresis. Escalation: On-call SRE (Diego) and Platform Eng (Lina Park) engaged.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a PaperTrail Labs dedicated API key and open N concurrent streaming sessions (N ~ 250 in us-east) with short keepalive and frequent small messages (simulate chat heartbeats).
2) Interleave small non-streaming inference calls at a QPS spike to create mixed workloads (example: 500 QPS of 100-token generation calls).
3) Observe gateway return rates and runtime logs as load ramps quickly over ~60s.
4) Trigger client-side retry within 200-500ms (aggressive retry) to emulate observed client behavior and look for accept queue growth and 502/503 patterns.

investigation_notes: Checked Grafana dashboard: /d/platform/ingress?var-tenant=papertrail -> saw correlated spikes in accept-queue length and gateway 5xx around 03:40 UTC.
Datadog traces show many short lived connections; p95 connect time spiked from 12ms -> 480ms during the window.
Replayed load in staging with identical throttler params reproduced downstream watchdog timeouts when client retry jitter < 100ms.
Heap and GPU metrics on dedicated pool were in normal range; issue reproduced without GPU pressure, pointing to socket/backlog and scheduler pressure as proximate cause.

Reviewed recent deploys: ingress throttler tuning rolled 2026-03-09 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/1192) and runtime retry jitter patch 2026-03-08 (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567).
comments: Ava Chen (Support): Customer reported reconnect storms at ~03:38 UTC; sending initial logs and asked SRE to triage.
Diego Martinez (SRE): Looking at accept-queue metrics now; suspected token-bucket rejects leading to retry storms. Lowered per-route cap as temporary mitigation.
Lina Park (Platform Eng): Noted runtime retry jitter change in last release; will run staged replay to validate interaction with throttler.
PaperTrail Support Rep (customer): Confirming their SDK had default retry 300ms with no jitter; asking whether recommended SDK changes exist.
Diego Martinez (SRE): Action: reverted per-tenant throttler tuning from 2026-03-09 and increased keepalive pool by 30% for this tenant. Monitoring impact.
resolution: Temporary fix: rolled back ingress throttler parameter change and increased per-route keepalive pool; advised customer to enable client-side jittered exponential backoff (recommended SDK patch v2.3.1).
Patch delivered: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4589 introduces 20-300ms randomized jitter in runtime retry logic and guards against concentrated reconnects.
Autoscaler change: follow-up ticket created to add socket/accept-queue as an autoscaling signal (INT-332101).
Follow-up: schedule postmortem and runbook update; add chaos test in staging to validate throttler hysteresis behavior under mixed streaming+short-call workloads.
